title: King John Seals Magna Carta at Runnymede
dek: On 15 June 1215 rebel barons force King John to seal a Great Charter at a Thames meadow. Its clauses on lawful judgment and limits on arbitrary rule become England's template for constitutional restraint.
body: Neither side kept faith, the pope annulled it, and civil war followed; reissues under Henry III and Edward I turned the failed peace into England's constitutional template.

panels.label: Later Readers Said
panels.text: Sir Edward Coke and later lawyers treated Magna Carta as the foundation of English liberty against arbitrary kings, and Lord Denning called it the greatest constitutional document of all time.

panels.label: Medievalists Said
panels.text: J. C. Holt and later historians said the 1215 charter was a feudal peace deal among barons and a king, and that the story of universal rights was invented centuries afterward.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: Both camps still quote the same parchment; at stake is whether Magna Carta binds as living liberty law or as a medieval settlement remade by later politics.
